mental_model: After bufferization, MarkStrideAlign walks each device function and decides, for every on-chip buffer an HIVM structured op touches, which dimension's stride must be padded so strided hardware accesses stay aligned to the 32-byte vector block; each decision is recorded as an annotation mark carrying a dimension list and a byte count. It rewrites nothing else — the marks are a contract handed to the enable-stride-align pass, which performs the actual re-allocation.
need: On Ascend vector/block hardware, a strided access whose inter-row stride is not a multiple of the hardware alignment unit (32 bytes for UB/L1) either fails or is slow; some DMA/fixpipe modes additionally require specific N/M-stride multiples. Somebody must decide where those padding requirements apply and record them, but the decision needs op-level knowledge (which axis is discontinuous, which mode the DMA uses) that the allocator does not have.
responsibility: For every HIVM structured op with on-chip (non-GM) memref operands — and, on RegBase, every vf-call argument — decide whether a stride-align requirement exists, which dimension it applies to, and how many bytes it requires, then attach that decision as an annotation mark on the buffer value; refuse loudly (pass failure) when the IR is not bufferized memref.
observable_outcome: A module whose IR shape and types are unchanged except for new annotation.mark ops placed after buffer values, each carrying hivm.stride_align_dims = array<i32: dim...> and hivm.stride_align_value_in_byte = array<i32: bytes...> (e.g. {hivm.stride_align_dims = array<i32: 1>, hivm.stride_align_value_in_byte = array<i32: 32>}); buffers that need no alignment get no mark.

audience_contract.who: compiler engineers familiar with MLIR passes and bufferization who have never read the AlignBuffer directory
audience_contract.assumed_knowledge: MLIR pass pipelines, memref layouts/strides, what bufferization produces
audience_contract.not_assumed: Ascend memory spaces (UB/L1/L0C), fixpipe DMA modes, this pass's internals

triggers.interaction: alignStoragePipeline adds PreMarkStrideAlign and MarkStrideAlign only when this option is true; when false both passes are skipped entirely (EnableStrideAlign still runs and simply finds nothing to do)

upstream.interaction: produces the memref-world IR the pass requires: hivm structured ops with pure buffer semantics, strided memref layouts, UB/L1 address spaces, and concrete alloc shapes

upstream.entity: PreMarkStrideAlign (hivm-pre-mark-stride-align, run immediately before in the same pipeline)
upstream.interaction: pre-marks DMA-loaded buffers whose data will be vload'd in vector functions with skip_stride_align_for_vload on the root alloc; MarkStrideAlign consults this in both walks and skips those buffers, because stride padding would create inter-row gaps that vldsx1 cannot load

upstream.entity: HIVM structured ops (hivm.hir.load/store/copy, elementwise ops, fixpipe, custom ops) with UB/L1/L0C memref operands
upstream.interaction: provide the shapes, strides, address spaces, and mode attributes (dma_mode, dual-dst, tightly-coupled-buffer tiling_dim) from which the align decision is computed

downstream.entity: EnableStrideAlign (hivm-enable-stride-align, ModuleOp, runs right after memref FoldAllocReshape in the same alignStoragePipeline)
downstream.interaction: consumes the marks verbatim: validates dims/bytes presence and equal length, propagates them up to root allocs and down to leaf operands, then re-allocates each marked alloc with padded static dims and a strided subview of the original shape

downstream.entity: HIVM decompose phases named around stride alignment (BEFORE/AFTER_HIVM_STRIDE_ALIGNMENT), InferHIVMDataLayout, and ConvertHIVMToStandard (isOpsAligned = enableHIVMAutoStorageAlign)
downstream.interaction: the pipeline orders other passes around the mark/enable pair, and the conversion pass is told whether storage alignment happened

inputs.name: post-bufferization device function
inputs.form: func::FuncOp (non-host) containing HIVM structured ops on ranked memrefs with identity or strided layouts in UB/L1/L0C address spaces
inputs.description: host functions are skipped at entry; tensor-typed operands and ops without pure buffer semantics are errors, not input shapes

inputs.name: architecture context
inputs.form: archIsRegbased (isRegBasedArch) and archIs950 (isAscend950) read from the parent module's hacc.target
inputs.description: module-level target info; selects the regbase vs A2/A3 decision path and the fixpipe/950 special cases

inputs.name: PreMarkStrideAlign veto marks
inputs.form: annotation.mark ops carrying skip_stride_align_for_vload on alloc-like roots of DMA-loaded, vload-bound buffers
inputs.description: produced by the preceding pass; presence means 'do not mark this buffer'

outputs.name: annotation marks on buffer values
outputs.form: annotation.mark ops inserted immediately after the marked value, with dense-i32 arrays hivm.stride_align_dims (which dimension's stride) and hivm.stride_align_value_in_byte (required stride multiple in bytes)
outputs.description: default byte value is getHWAlignBytes(UB|L1) = BL = VL/8 = 32; fixpipe cases use per-mode table values; vsstb cases use (16*N+1)*element-width bytes; no mark where no requirement exists

mechanism.summary: Five source-derived stages: gate and traverse the function's HIVM structured ops; decide whether the op/buffer needs a mark at all; compute the align dimension per architecture path; refine the decision per op kind; emit the annotation mark (or skip silently), with a parallel call-argument walk on RegBase.

stages.name: Gate & traverse
stages.what: skip host functions; capture regbase/950 architecture flags; walk ops keeping only HIVMStructuredOps whose operands are not all-GM; handle CustomOp/CustomMacroOp from per-arg align_dim argAttrs; require pure buffer semantics (else error)

stages.name: Filter candidate ops
stages.what: skip last-dim transposes (alloc size already aligned), regbase reduce-with-index, all-rank-0 types, ops without a local (UB/L1/L0C) buffer; classify UB DMA ops (Load/Store/Copy) for later shortcuts

stages.name: Compute the align dimension
stages.what: regbase: drop all-ones shapes (except fixpipe), keep only UB-space memref types, build identity reassociation (A5 flatten already merged axes) and call getLastDiscontinuousDimRegBased — non-unit last-dim stride aligns the last non-unit axis; UB DMA ops with sub-low strides already aligned take a no-mark shortcut; fixpipe uses dtype/mode constraint tables for N and M strides and marks the root alloc for 3d-dot tiles; A2/A3 instead flattens via FlattenInterface and calls getLastDiscontinuousDim

stages.name: Choose the mark target & refine
stages.what: take the op's UB target-space operands; for a single-UB-operand StoreOp whose operand is a trailing-unit rank-reduced subview, remap the align dim into result coordinates or retarget the mark to the subview source; skip operands whose root carries PreMarkStrideAlign's skip_stride_align_for_vload; refine the dim with adjustAlignDim, which drops marks for scalar-loop-lowered ops and implicit-transpose load/store and applies brc/reduce/deinterleave/copy special cases

stages.name: Emit marks (or fail loudly)
stages.what: markAlignedDim validates memref legality (ranked, identity/strided layout, dim in range) and creates the annotation mark with the dimension and byte count (default getHWAlignBytes = 32 for UB/L1); a second regbase-only walk does the same for vf-call arguments (skipping already-marked and non-i1 operands on 950) and adds vsstb bank-conflict marks for suitable transfer-writes in callees; any legality error interrupts the walk and the pass signals failure

control_flow: the regbase pipeline (alignStoragePipeline) drives the pass once per function, gated by enableHIVMAutoStorageAlign, immediately after PreMarkStrideAlign
runOnOperation drives two full function walks in order: the structured-op walk, then (regbase only) the func.call-argument walk; each walk may mark, skip, or (on legality errors) interrupt
interruption from either walk becomes signalPassFailure; everything else is silent skip
the pass is the only writer in its stage: it only inserts annotation ops, and the consumer pass in the same pipeline performs all real rewriting
data_flow: decision inputs: operand memref types (shape/stride/layout/memory space) + op mode attributes (fixpipe dma_mode/dual-dst/tiling_dim, custom-op align_dim) + architecture flags -> (alignDim, alignBytes)
mark output: (alignDim, alignBytes) -> annotation.mark op after the buffer value (op operands, subview sources on the store fixup, alloc results for fixpipe 3d-dot, call operands for vf args)
veto input: PreMarkStrideAlign's skip_stride_align_for_vload mark on the traced root -> operand excluded from marking
the marks flow to EnableStrideAlign, which unions and propagates them along the value graph before re-allocating

provenance.source: bishengir/test/Dialect/HIVM/hivm-mark-stride-align-fixcctoub.mlir (CHECK expectations recorded from the fixture at HEAD 90037fe33; NOT executed in this analysis — runtime_verification is none)

canonical_example.initial_state: func.func @test_nsize_b16_cs_n_nd_n_le_n (AIC core, Ascend950PR_9579): %alloc = memref.alloc() : memref<16x16xf16, #hivm.address_space<ub>> carrying a tightly-coupled-buffer mark, written by hivm.hir.fixpipe from an L0C (cc) alloc; no stride_align mark exists yet
canonical_example.inputs: -hivm-mark-stride-align (no pass options; the pass has none — behavior is selected by pipeline gate and architecture)
execution_trace: Gate & traverse: AIC func is not host; the fixpipe is an HIVMStructuredOp with a non-GM (UB) operand; buffer semantics are pure

Compute the align dimension: regbase path; fixpipe branch reads dma_mode (none -> ND/DN defaults), channel split (none), data width f16 -> B16; table row {B16, NZ2DN N, DualDst N} gives nSizeStride 16 elements
Emit: alignBytes = 16 * 16 bits / 8 = 32; markAlignedDimForFixcctoub targets the UB output operand %alloc
createAlignMarkOp inserts annotation.mark after %alloc with {hivm.stride_align_dims = array<i32: 1>, hivm.stride_align_value_in_byte = array<i32: 32>}
important_states: before the pass: %alloc has effects/tightly_coupled_buffer marks only
after the pass: %alloc additionally carries the stride-align mark with dim 1 and 32 bytes; nothing else in the function changed
canonical_example.result: AIC: annotation.mark %alloc {hivm.stride_align_dims = array<i32: 1>, hivm.stride_align_value_in_byte = array<i32: 32>} — exactly the fixture's CHECK line (:5); the companion negative case (fixture test 25) shows that a buffer whose last-dim stride is already 32 bytes gets AIC-NOT: annotation.mark
boundary_examples: downstream effect of the same mark shape: a hand-written mark {dim 1, 32 bytes} on a memref<2x15xf16, ub> alloc leads -hivm-enable-stride-align to produce a padded memref<2x15x16xf16> alloc plus a strided<[240, 16]> subview (propagate-scope fixture, EV-018)
mark target fixup: a single-UB-operand store through a trailing-unit rank-reduced subview may retarget the mark to the subview source so propagation sees the true semantic axis (EV-010)
veto path: the same buffer marked skip_stride_align_for_vload by PreMarkStrideAlign receives no stride-align mark (EV-020)

state_transitions.before: hivm structured op on UB buffers, no stride_align marks anywhere on the operands
state_transitions.operation: compute (dim, bytes), insert annotation.mark after each UB target-space operand (or the subview source on the store fixup)
state_transitions.after: each marked value has one annotation.mark carrying hivm.stride_align_dims + hivm.stride_align_value_in_byte; op/types unchanged
state_transitions.reason: the decision must live on the value so the consumer can propagate it to the root alloc

state_transitions.before: L0C->UB fixpipe writing a 2-D UB alloc (e.g. 16x16 f16, nz2nd)
state_transitions.operation: look up N/M stride requirements in the dtype/mode tables; mark all UB target-space operands (and the root alloc for 3d-dot tiles)
state_transitions.after: alloc carries e.g. {dim 1, 32 bytes} (B16/N:16) or {dim 1, 16 bytes} (B8/N:16); already-aligned strides produce no mark
state_transitions.reason: fixpipe DMA modes hard-require specific N/M stride multiples the generic dim finder cannot express

state_transitions.operation: skip already-marked operands, compute align dim from continuous reassociations, mark; then markForVsstb adds bank-conflict marks for transfer-write-suitable callee inputs
state_transitions.after: vf call operands (and vsstb candidates at rank-2 with (16N+1)*width bytes) carry marks; operands the callee vloads stay unmarked (veto)
state_transitions.reason: vf arguments are buffers the structured-op walk does not see, and vsstb stores slow down on conflicting bank strides

state_transitions.before: marks scattered on leaf values (op operands, subviews, allocs)
state_transitions.operation: EnableStrideAlign normalizes, propagates marks up to root allocations and down to leaves, unions per-op, re-allocates with padded dims
state_transitions.after: padded alloc + strided subview replace the original alloc; the original mark contract is fully consumed
state_transitions.reason: the mark is an intermediate representation of a layout requirement, not the layout change itself

decisions.question: Does this op/buffer need a stride-align mark at all?
decisions.condition: op kind, operand address spaces, shapes and existing strides; plus the PreMarkStrideAlign veto
outcomes: no local (UB/L1/L0C) buffer, all-GM operands, all-rank-0, all-ones shape (non-fixpipe), host func -> no mark
last-dim transpose (alloc size already aligned), regbase reduce-with-index, scalar-loop-lowered ops, implicit-transpose load/store -> no mark
UB DMA op whose sub-low strides are already aligned (isSubLowDimStrideAlign && isNotTailJumpOrStrideAlign) -> no mark
last-dim stride already a multiple of the align value (fixture test 25) -> no mark
buffer root carries skip_stride_align_for_vload -> no mark, protecting vldsx1 vloads
decisions.reason: marking is only correct where a requirement exists; the veto marks exist because a wrong mark would break vload contiguity

decisions.question: Which dimension's stride must be aligned?
decisions.condition: layout/strides of the UB memref types and the op's reassociation (identity on regbase post-flatten; FlattenInterface on A2/A3)
outcomes: any operand with non-unit last-dim stride -> the last non-unit axis (getLastNotUnitDim)
UB DMA op with already-aligned sub-low strides -> none (shortcut)
multi-dim, unit-stride last dim -> the last discontinuous dim from the reassociation
fixpipe -> trailing reassociation index (N) and/or second-to-last (M) from the mode tables; 3d-dot tiles also align root-alloc dim 1
decisions.reason: the hardware requirement is about the stride of a non-innermost (discontinuous) axis, not the innermost contiguous one

decisions.question: How many bytes must the stride be aligned to?
decisions.condition: memory space of the marked buffer; op-specific tables
outcomes: fixpipe: per-(dtype, channel-split, NZ2ND/NZ2DN, loop-enhance, dual-dst) table entries converted as elements * dataWidth / 8 (e.g. 16, 32, 64 bytes)
vsstb bank-conflict: (shape[rank-2] * 16 / gcd(shape[rank-2], 16) + 1) * element byte width, i.e. the 512*N+32 byte Davinci recommendation in elements
custom ops: per-arg align_dim from argAttrs with the default byte value
decisions.reason: the byte value is the hardware contract being encoded into the mark

decisions.question: Which value gets the mark, and what happens on illegal IR?
decisions.condition: the op's UB target-space operands; store-through-subview shape; type/layout legality
outcomes: each UB target-space operand is marked in place
single-UB-operand store through a trailing-unit rank-reduced subview -> dim remapped to result coordinates, or the mark retargeted to the subview source
tensor-typed operand, unranked memref, non-identity/non-strided layout, or dim out of range -> emitError and interrupt -> signalPassFailure
decisions.reason: the mark must sit where propagation to the root alloc sees the right semantic axis; illegal IR must fail the compile rather than silently drop the alignment requirement

constraints.statement: the pass only accepts bufferized IR: tensor-typed operands and ops without pure buffer semantics are hard errors ('Not bufferized.') that fail the pass
marked memrefs must be ranked with identity or strided layout; anything else ('UnrankedMemRef not supported.', 'Non-strided-memref not supported.') fails the pass
the align dim must be within the memref rank ('align dim is too large.')
marks are only ever created on UB (on-chip) values: candidates are filtered to local buffers and, on regbase, to UB address space; GM-only ops are skipped
mark arrays must be equal-length (dims vs bytes) for the consumer to accept them; the producer guarantees this by construction (one dim per byte value per createAlignMarkOp call)
buffers vetoed by PreMarkStrideAlign (vload'd DMA loads in VFs) must not be marked, because stride padding would break vldsx1's 128-element consecutive load

invariants.statement: the pass never rewrites ops, types, or layouts — it only inserts annotation.mark ops; the module's semantics before/after differ only by metadata
each mark is inserted immediately after the value it annotates, so the (dim, bytes) pair travels with the value and EnableStrideAlign can trace it through view-like ops to the root alloc
the default stride-align unit for UB/L1 buffers is the hardware vector block: BL = VL/8 = 32 bytes

assumptions.statement: on the regbase path, hfusion-flatten has already merged axes before this pass runs, so the identity reassociation is the correct view of the operand layout (in-code comment: 'In A5, memrefTypes is already the result of flattening')

the fixpipe N/M stride tables enumerate the modes the hardware requires; a mode missing from the tables yields no mark (lookup returns -1), which the code treats as 'no requirement' rather than an error

boundaries.statement: HIVM structured ops with UB/L1/L0C memref operands on the regbase path (identity reassociation + UB DMA shortcuts + fixpipe tables), vf-call arguments on regbase (incl. vsstb bank-conflict marks), and A2/A3 structured ops implementing FlattenInterface

tensor (pre-bufferization) IR and ops without pure buffer semantics are errors; vload'd DMA buffers, implicit-transpose load/store, scalar-loop-lowered ops, last-dim transposes, and regbase reduce-with-index are deliberately not marked

vsstb bank-conflict marking refuses operands used by memref.collapse_shape/memref.reshape — the in-code TODO notes padding would create discontinuous shapes those users cannot handle, so such operands stay unmarked
custom macros/ops without per-arg align_dim entries in argAttrs get nothing from that path; there is no pass option to force a mark — behavior is fully decided by the IR and the architecture

the exact marks the generic structured-op path would choose for arbitrary kernels were not observed: the reviewed corpus only runs -hivm-mark-stride-align on fixpipe fixtures; other stride-align tests hand-author the producer marks

placement.why_here: it sits in alignStoragePipeline (HIVMRegbasePipelines.cpp:485-494) right after AlignAllocSize and PreMarkStrideAlign and before memref FoldAllocReshape + EnableStrideAlign, inside hivmPostBufferizationOptimizationPipeline (called at :560), i.e. after bufferizationPipeline (:695) in buildLowerHIVMPipelines (:699) — exactly when buffer decisions (types, strides, address spaces, allocs) are final but the consumer can still rewrite allocations
placement.why_not_earlier: pre-bufferization the operands are tensors: markAlignedDim and the buffer-semantics check turn tensor IR into a pass failure, and neither strided memref layouts nor the allocs to be padded exist yet
placement.why_not_later: the whole downstream sequence — FoldAllocReshape, EnableStrideAlign's re-allocation, the AFTER_HIVM_STRIDE_ALIGNMENT decompose phase, InferHIVMDataLayout — depends on the marks existing; moving the pass later would leave the consumer re-allocating from stale or missing requirements

key_takeaways: MarkStrideAlign is the producer half of a two-pass contract: it computes where stride alignment is required (which buffer, which dimension, how many bytes) and records it as pure metadata — annotation.mark ops with hivm.stride_align_dims + hivm.stride_align_value_in_byte — changing nothing else.

The mark's default byte value is the hardware vector block BL = VL/8 = 32 bytes for UB/L1 buffers; fixpipe DMA modes override it with per-(dtype, mode) table values, and vsstb store inputs get bank-conflict strides of (16N+1) elements.

It must run post-bufferization by construction: tensor IR is a hard error, and its decision inputs (strided memref layouts, UB address space, concrete allocs) only exist in the memref world — it sits in alignStoragePipeline between PreMarkStrideAlign and EnableStrideAlign, inside the regbase post-bufferization pipeline.

EnableStrideAlign can rely on: marks present only where a requirement exists, dims/bytes arrays of equal length, marks placed immediately after the buffer value, and no marks on vload'd DMA buffers (PreMarkStrideAlign's skip_stride_align_for_vload veto) — it validates the first two and fails loudly if violated.

Failure is loud, skipping is silent: legality violations (tensor, unranked, non-strided layout, dim out of range) interrupt the walk and signal pass failure, while 'no requirement here' simply emits no mark.

pass.pass_arg: func::FuncOp — def MarkStrideAlign : Pass<"hivm-mark-stride-align", "func::FuncOp"> (Passes.td:876-886); the pipeline instantiates it with pm.nest<func::FuncOp>().addPass(createMarkStrideAlignPass()); no pass-level options
pass.operation_scope: one device (non-host) function per invocation: walk 1 covers HIVM structured ops with non-GM memref operands (plus CustomOp/CustomMacroOp align_dim args); walk 2 (regbase only) covers func.call arguments feeding vf callees; module-level context (hacc.target) selects the architecture path

pipeline_placements.position: alignStoragePipeline step 2 of 4: AlignAllocSize -> [PreMarkStrideAlign -> MarkStrideAlign] -> memref FoldAllocReshape -> EnableStrideAlign (HIVMRegbasePipelines.cpp:485-494, marks at :488-490)
same slot but without PreMarkStrideAlign: AlignAllocSize -> MarkStrideAlign -> FoldAllocReshape -> EnableStrideAlign (HIVMPipelines.cpp:377-384)
pipeline_placements.gate: the same enableHIVMAutoStorageAlign option; ConvertHIVMToStandard is told via isOpsAligned (HIVMPipelines.cpp:539-543)

ir_contract.before: post-bufferization memref IR: hivm structured ops with pure buffer semantics on ranked memrefs (identity or strided layout) in UB/L1/L0C address spaces; no stride_align annotations on the buffers it will mark
ir_contract.after: identical IR plus inserted annotation.mark ops placed directly after the marked buffer values, each carrying {hivm.stride_align_dims = array<i32: dim...>, hivm.stride_align_value_in_byte = array<i32: bytes...>}; zero ops rewritten, zero types changed; buffers with no requirement carry no mark

attributes.creator: creates annotation.mark ops carrying hivm.stride_align_dims and hivm.stride_align_value_in_byte (HIVMAttrs.td:1265-1276) — the 'stride align marks' of the pass summary; reads (never writes) hivm.skip_stride_align_for_vload, custom-op argAttrs align_dim, fixpipe dma_mode/dual-dst, and hivm.tiling_dim on tightly-coupled-buffer marks
attributes.consumer: EnableStrideAlign consumes stride_align_dims/stride_align_value_in_byte as its sole steering input: it validates them, propagates them up to root allocs and down to leaves, unions them per op, and re-allocates marked allocs with padded static dims (EnableStrideAlign.cpp:61-80, 131-161, 359-445); the downstream hivm.storage_aligned func attr is set by the consumer on membase only

pass.legality: hard requirements (violation = pass failure): bufferized pure-buffer-semantics ops, ranked memref, identity/strided layout, align dim within rank. Silent skip (no mark): host funcs; all-GM operands; no local buffer; all-rank-0; all-ones shape (except fixpipe); last-dim transpose; regbase reduce-with-index; scalar-loop-lowered ops; implicit-transpose load/store; UB DMA with already-aligned sub-low strides; stride already aligned (fixture test 25); skip_stride_align_for_vload veto; collapse_shape/reshape users of vsstb candidates
pass.rewrite: none in the layout sense — annotation-only emission via createAlignMarkOp (PropagateAlignUtil.cpp:1777-1790); the physical transformation (padded alloc + strided subview + type propagation through view-like ops) belongs entirely to EnableStrideAlign
